name: The Lost Pages
summary: A gust has scattered The Lost Pages across Ashenvale. Gurda Ragescar is stranded near Splintertree Post, unable to run the shredder she is taking from Ratchet to the Warsong Lumber Camp without its manual.

sections.title: A Gust of Bad Luck
sections.body: The Warsong Clan uses steam-powered shredders bought from Ratchet to clear lumber across Ashenvale. Their delicate workings are not easy for an orc warrior to master. As Gurda Ragescar carried a newly bought shredder north, a sudden gust tore the instruction booklet from her hands. Twelve parchment leaves scattered across the forest floor.

sections.title: Pages in the Wilderness
sections.body: The wind carried the manual pages across Ashenvale, and wandering creatures, cultists, and forest denizens have taken them. The shredder cannot run without all three chapters. Gurda is stranded on the road to Splintertree Post, unable to report for logging duty.

faq.answer: Gurda Ragescar is a Horde laborer carrying a goblin shredder from Ratchet to Ashenvale for the Warsong Lumber Camp's logging work.

faq.q: Why does Gurda need an instruction manual to drive the shredder?
faq.answer: Goblin machinery is finicky and hard to understand. Even an eager orc cannot safely operate the shredder without its manufacturer's manual.

faq.q: How did the manual pages end up scattered all over Ashenvale?
faq.answer: A violent gust tore the book from Gurda's grasp as she traveled north along the forest road. Its loose pages scattered through the woods, leaving her with only the empty front cover.

faq.q: Where does the shredder ultimately belong?
faq.answer: The shredder is bound for the Warsong Lumber Camp, where the Horde cuts timber to supply Orgrimmar and Durotar.

faq.q: Where can the missing pages be found?
faq.answer: The pages have spread across Ashenvale and been picked up by humanoids and hostile forest denizens roaming the region.

faq.q: Why does the Horde purchase machinery from Ratchet?
faq.answer: Ratchet is the nearest neutral port with trade links to goblin cartels. The Horde buys specialized engineering, demolition tools, and steam-driven vehicles there for its military logistics.

angles.text: As an engineer, you can understand Gurda's trouble: running a goblin shredder without its maker's instructions risks a boiler failure.
As a member of the Horde, you know each shredder at the Warsong Lumber Camp helps gather timber for walls, huts, and warships in Durotar.
As an orc, you may share Gurda's frustration with lost technical pages; manual labor and warrior traditions leave little patience for goblin paperwork.
